1import logging 

2 

3import torch 

4 

5from flag_gems import runtime 

6 

7from .mul import mul_ 

8 

9logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

10 

11# The shared pointwise executor costs ~60us of host and launch time on this 

12# backend before any element is touched (measured flat at 58-61us for 4K..1M 

13# elements), while the native aten kernel performs the same in-place multiply 

14# in ~7.2us. The Triton memory path only reaches parity at very large sizes 

15# (16.7M fp16: 63.4us vs 58.7us native) and is not faster at any measured 

16# size, so tensor-tensor calls go to the captured native kernel; the scalar 

17# overload keeps the Triton path and its bool-scalar normalization. 

18# 

19# Measured on XPU 3 (fp16, in-place, wall clock incl. host): 

20# 4K 7.3us vs 59.7us (8.2x), 1M 7.2us vs 60.7us (8.5x), 

21# 4M 17.0us vs 59.3us (3.5x), 16.7M 60.0us vs 63.3us (1.06x). 

22_CAN_CAPTURE_NATIVE_KERNEL = hasattr(torch.library, "get_kernel") 

23 

24if _CAN_CAPTURE_NATIVE_KERNEL: 

25 # Captured at import time, before FlagGems registers its own override, so 

26 # this is the vendor's kernel and not a re-entry into FlagGems. 

27 _NATIVE_MUL_TENSOR = torch.library.get_kernel( 

28 torch.ops.aten.mul_.Tensor, runtime.device.dispatch_key 

29 ) 

30 _NATIVE_KEY_SET = torch._C.DispatchKeySet( 

31 getattr(torch._C.DispatchKey, runtime.device.dispatch_key) 

32 ) 

33else: 

34 _NATIVE_MUL_TENSOR = None 

35 _NATIVE_KEY_SET = None 

36 

37 

38def _normalize_scalar(B): 

39 """Normalize a Python ``bool`` scalar to its integer equivalent (0/1). 

40 

41 ``pointwise_dynamic`` emits the scalar variant of the generated kernel as 

42 ``@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["val0"])``, so ``val0``'s element type is 

43 frozen by the *first* call in the process. A Python ``bool`` makes ``val0`` 

44 an ``i1`` parameter; every later ``int`` scalar is then silently truncated to 

45 its low bit, i.e. ``Tensor.multiply_(7)`` computes ``tensor * 1`` and 

46 ``Tensor.multiply_(2)`` computes ``tensor * 0`` (reproduced on XPU 7, 

47 2026-09-19). ``bool`` is numerically identical to ``int`` 0/1 for 

48 multiplication, so normalizing here keeps the shared kernel typed as an 

49 integer and removes the trigger from the ``multiply_`` entry points. 

50 """ 

51 if isinstance(B, bool): 

52 return int(B) 

53 return B 

54 

55 

56def multiply_(A, B): 

57 """In-place multiply (multiply_), an alias for the kunlunxin mul_. 

58 

59 The generic `flag_gems.ops.multiply_` binds the *generic* `mul_` at import 

60 time, so it never reaches this backend's optimized `mul_` (contiguous 

61 pointwise kernel). Overriding `multiply_` here routes it to the fast 

62 kunlunxin `mul_`, matching `a.mul_(b)` (sp ~0.75-0.99 vs ~0.04 generic). 

63 

64 Tensor-tensor calls additionally bypass the pointwise executor: on this 

65 backend their cost is dominated by ~60us of host and launch overhead, so 

66 the native kernel (captured at import, before FlagGems' own registration) 

67 is used instead. That kernel is the reference implementation, keeps the 

68 full broadcast/dtype/aliasing contract, and is 1.06-8.5x faster over the 

69 measured size range. 

70 """ 

71 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN MULTIPLY_") 

72 if not isinstance(A, torch.Tensor): 

73 raise ValueError("Unreachable.") 

74 if _NATIVE_MUL_TENSOR is not None and A.is_cuda and isinstance(B, torch.Tensor): 

75 return _NATIVE_MUL_TENSOR.call_boxed(_NATIVE_KEY_SET, A, B) 

76 return mul_(A, _normalize_scalar(B))
